newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks finish Friday with broad advance.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks finish Friday with broad advance.

text.p: U.S. stocks rallied Friday on data indicating moderate economic growth, which for the moment pushed aside concerns about the imminent deluge of quarterly earnings news.

The advance came on the sixth anniversary of Wall Street's bull market, and ended four consecutive losing sessions while reviving expectations the Dow Jones Industrial Average was on the way to residing above 6000.
The Dow finished up 48 at 5969 with gainers ahead of decliners by about seven to four.

Other market barometers gained: the S&P 500 rose six to 701, the Nasdaq composite grew 11 to 1248 -- reflecting particularly vigorous buying in technology stocks -- and the New York Stock Exchange composite improved 2.5 to 373.
Meanwhile, the price on 30-year treasury bond climbed 1/2 a point to yield 6.85 percent.
For the week, the Dow shed almost 24 points.
The blue-chip reading cracked 6000 briefly after Monday's market open, and on Tuesday it reached 6010, but both days finished with declines.

"It has been a very powerful market today. We were hitting on all cyliners and what launched it was the combination of good retail sales and a good wholesale inflation number," said Hugh Johnson, First Albany Corp chief investment officer.
In September, wholesale prices grew 0.2 percent, just under expectations, while the core rate which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3 percent, slightly more than expected.
Retail sales increased 0.7 percent last month, well beyond forecasts, but the report included a downward revision of August sales to a 0.2 percent decline.
The economic data was released one hour before the stock market open, an interval that saw bonds rally on the news while equity investors geared for heavy buying.
Technology stocks -- especially semiconductors -- Wall Street brokerages and retailer were among the strongest groups of the day, while precious metal issues suffered.
Morgan Stanley set a positive tone for the chip stocks with an upgrade this morning of Intel Corp to strong buy from outperform.
Intel is expected to announce its quarterly results on Monday.
The analyst also raised the earnings estimates for the quarter ended in September and for each quarter through the end of fiscal 1997.
For the latest period, the new earnings outlook is $1.31 per share, up from $1.19.
Intel shares jumped 5-1/2 to 105-3/8, threatening the 12-month high 107 notched on Tuesday.

"It was a real barnburner of a day for the technology sector because with tightness in the labor and capital markets, companies are investing in capacity-enhancing technology, so most economists are now revising upward their forecasts for technology spending," Johnson said.
Texas Instruments Inc rose 1/4 to 55-3/8, Motorola Inc advanced 1/2 to 48-3/4, Atmel Corp added 1-1/4 to 31-3/8, Applied Materials was up 3/8 to 29-3/4.
Also, International Business Machines Corp closed at 130-1/8 -- a new year-high -- up 2-3/8.

The Nasdaq's most active issue Cascade Communications Corp was hammered after reporting quarterly results that exceeded Wall Street expectations, but disappointed nonetheless because of a slimmer-than-expected rise versus the prior quarterly results.
Cascade fell 15-1/8, a 17.5 percent loss, to close at 71-3/8 after almost 16 million shares changed hands.
-- Wall Street Desk, 212-859-1734.
